aciklama: The following material has been prepared based on the Noble Qur'an and major hadith collections. The grades of narrations are indicated in the relevant entries; an effort has been made to exclude narrations known to be clearly weak or fabricated.

dualar.baslik: Surah al-Fatihah (Fâtiha Sûresi)
dualar.arapca: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ ﴿١﴾ الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ ﴿٢﴾ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ ﴿٣﴾ مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ ﴿٤﴾ إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ ﴿٥﴾ اهْدِنَا الصِّرَاطَ الْمُسْتَقِيمَ ﴿٦﴾ صِرَاطَ الَّذِينَ أَنْعَمْتَ عَلَيْهِمْ غَيْرِ الْمَغْضُوبِ عَلَيْهِمْ وَلَا الضَّالِّينَ
dualar.okunus: Bismillâhi'r-rahmâni'r-rahîm. Elhamdü lillâhi rabbi'l-âlemîn. Er-rahmâni'r-rahîm. Mâliki yevmi'd-dîn. İyyâke na'büdü ve iyyâke neste'în. İhdine's-sırâta'l-müstakîm. Sırâtallezîne en'amte aleyhim ğayri'l-mağdûbi aleyhim ve le'd-dâllîn.
dualar.anlam: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate. Praise belongs to Allah, the Lord of the worlds, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, the Master of the Day of Judgment. You alone we serve and worship, and You alone we ask for help and support. O Lord, guide us to the straight path, the path of those blessed people upon whom You have bestowed Your favor, not the path of those who have incurred Your anger or those who have gone astray.
dualar.kaynak: The Noble Qur'an (Elmalılı Hamdi Yazır translation)
dualar.tekrar: Optional; may be recited daily
dualar.neZaman: At any time, with the intention of seeking healing, protection, and guidance
dualar.aciklama: Surah al-Fatihah is described as the "mother/essence of the Qur'an" (Ümmü'l-Kur'an), and reciting it in every rak'ah of salah is obligatory. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "There is no salah for one who does not recite al-Fatihah" (Bukhari, Adhan, 95; Muslim, Salah, 41).
dualar.not: Surah al-Fatihah is a supplication asking Allah for guidance to the straight path and protection from going astray.

dualar.baslik: Ayat al-Kursi
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُ لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ ۚ لَا تَأْخُذُهُ سِنَةٌ وَلَا نَوْمٌ ۚ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ ۗ مَنْ ذَا الَّذِي يَشْفَعُ عِنْدَهُ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ ۚ يَعْلَمُ مَا بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ وَمَا خَلْفَهُمْ ۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيْءٍ مِنْ عِلْمِهِ إِلَّا بِمَا شَاءَ ۚ وَسِعَ كُرْسِيُّهُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ ۖ وَلَا يَئُودُهُ حِفْظُهُمَا ۚ وَهُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْعَظِيمُ
dualar.okunus: Allâhu lâ ilâhe illâ hüve'l-hayyü'l-kayyûm. Lâ te'huzühû sinetün ve lâ nevm. Lehû mâ fi's-semâvâti ve mâ fi'l-ard. Men ze'llezî yeşfe'u indehû illâ bi-iznih. Ya'lemü mâ beyne eydîhim ve mâ halfehüm. Ve lâ yühîtûne bi-şey'in min ilmihî illâ bi-mâ şâ'. Vesi'a kürsiyyühü's-semâvâti ve'l-ard. Ve lâ yeûdühû hıfzuhümâ. Ve hüve'l-aliyyü'l-azîm.
dualar.anlam: There is no deity but Allah. He is Ever-Living (hayydır), the Sustainer who governs all existence (kayyum). Neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes Him. Whatever is in the heavens and on earth belongs to Him. Who can intercede before Him without His permission? He knows all that lies before His servants and all that lies behind them. They can grasp nothing of His knowledge except what He wills. His Kursi encompasses all the heavens and the earth. Preserving and watching over them both does not burden Him. He is the Most High, the Most Great.
dualar.kaynak: The Noble Qur'an, Surah al-Baqarah 255 (Elmalılı Hamdi Yazır translation)
dualar.tekrar: Especially before going to sleep
dualar.neZaman: After every salah, at night and in the morning, before going to sleep
dualar.aciklama: It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ advised him to recite it for protection from devils and stated that whoever recites it at night will be protected by Allah until morning (Bukhari, Wakala, 10).
dualar.not: Reciting Ayat al-Kursi after every salah is also virtuous (Nasa'i, Amelü'l-yevm, 100).

dualar.baslik: Surah al-Baqarah, verses 285–286 (Âmenerrasûlü)
dualar.arapca: آمَنَ الرَّسُولُ بِمَا أُنْزِلَ إِلَيْهِ مِنْ رَبِّهِ وَالْمُؤْمِنُونَ ۚ كُلٌّ آمَنَ بِاللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ لَا نُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَحَدٍ مِنْ رُسُلِهِ ۚ وَقَالُوا سَمِعْنَا وَأَطَعْنَا ۖ غُفْرَانَكَ رَبَّنَا وَإِلَيْكَ الْمَصِيرُ ﴿۲۸۵﴾ لَا يُكَلِّفُ اللَّهُ نَفْسًا إِلَّا وُسْعَهَا ۚ لَهَا مَا كَسَبَتْ وَعَلَيْهَا مَا اكْتَسَبَتْ ۗ رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إِنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تَحْمِلْ عَلَيْنَا إِصْرًا كَمَا حَمَلْتَهُ عَلَى الَّذِينَ مِنْ قَبْلِنَا ۚ رَبَّنَا وَلَا تُحَمِّلْنَا مَا لَا طَاقَةَ لَنَا بِهِ ۖ وَاعْفُ عَنَّا وَاغْفِرْ لَنَا وَارْحَمْنَا ۚ أَنْتَ مَوْلَانَا فَانْصُرْنَا عَلَى الْقَوْمِ الْكَافِرِينَ
dualar.okunus: Âmenerrasûlü bimâ ünzile ileyhi min rabbihî vel-mü'minûn, küllün âmene billâhi ve melâiketihî ve kütübihî ve rusulih, lâ nüferriku beyne ehadin min rusulih, ve kâlû semi'nâ ve eta'nâ gufrâneke rabbenâ ve ileykel-masîr. Lâ yükellifullâhü nefsen illâ vus'ahâ, lehâ mâ kesebet ve aleyhâ mektesebet, rabbenâ lâ tüâhiznâ in nesînâ ev ahta'nâ, rabbenâ ve lâ tahmil aleynâ ısran kemâ hameltehû alellezîne min kablinâ, rabbenâ ve lâ tühammilnâ mâ lâ tâkate lenâ bih, va'fü annâ vağfir lenâ verhamnâ, ente mevlânâ fensurnâ alel-kavmil-kâfirîn.
dualar.anlam: The Messenger believed in what was revealed to him from his Lord. All the believers also believed in Allah, His angels, His books, and His messengers. They said, "We make no distinction among Allah's messengers. We hear and obey. Our Lord, we ask for Your forgiveness; to You alone is the return." Allah does not burden anyone beyond their capacity. Each person receives the good they have earned and bears the harm of the evil they have done. Our Lord, do not hold us accountable if we forget or make a mistake! Our Lord, do not place a heavy burden on us as You placed on those before us! Our Lord, do not burden us with what we cannot bear! Pardon us, forgive us, and have mercy on us! You are our Protector, so help us against the disbelieving people.
dualar.kaynak: The Noble Qur'an, Surah al-Baqarah 285–286 (Elmalılı Hamdi Yazır translation)
dualar.tekrar: Recommended to be recited when going to bed at night
dualar.neZaman: At night (especially before going to sleep)
dualar.aciklama: It is narrated from Abdullah b. Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) that these two verses are sufficient for whoever recites them at night (Bukhari, Tafsir, 2; Muslim, Musafirin, 257).
dualar.not: These two verses, known as "Âmenerrasûlü," are a means of protection for anyone who recites them before going to sleep at night.

dualar.baslik: Surah al-Ikhlas (Kul hüvellâhü ehad)
dualar.arapca: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ ﴿١﴾ اللَّهُ الصَّمَدُ ﴿٢﴾ لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ ﴿٣﴾ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌ
dualar.okunus: Kul hüvellâhü ehad. Allâhü's-samed. Lem yelid ve lem yûled. Ve lem yekün lehû küfüven ehad.
dualar.anlam: Say: He is Allah, the One. Allah is perfect and samed (all creation is in need of Him, but He is in need of nothing). He neither begot nor was He begotten. And there is none equal to Him.
dualar.kaynak: The Noble Qur'an (Elmalılı Hamdi Yazır translation)
dualar.tekrar: Three times a day (morning and evening), before going to sleep
dualar.neZaman: In the morning, in the evening, before going to sleep, at any time
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stated that this surah is equivalent to one third of the Qur'an (Bukhari, Fedâilü'l-Kur'ân, 13).
dualar.not: It is Sunnah to recite Surah al-Ikhlas three times each morning and evening for protection.

dualar.baslik: Surah al-Falaq (Kul e'ûzü birabbil felak)
dualar.arapca: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ الْفَلَقِ ﴿١﴾ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ ﴿٢﴾ وَمِنْ شَرِّ غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ ﴿٣﴾ وَمِنْ شَرِّ النَّفَّاثَاتِ فِي الْعُقَدِ ﴿٤﴾ وَمِنْ شَرِّ حَاسِدٍ إِذَا حَسَدَ
dualar.okunus: Kul e'ûzü birabbi'l-felak. Min şerri mâ halak. Ve min şerri ğasikın izâ vekab. Ve min şerri'n-neffâsâti fi'l-ukad. Ve min şerri hâsidin izâ hased.
dualar.anlam: Say: "I seek refuge in the Lord of daybreak from the evil of what He has created, from the evil of the night when its darkness falls, from the evil of magicians who blow on knots, and from the evil of the envier when they envy."
dualar.kaynak: The Noble Qur'an (Elmalılı Hamdi Yazır translation)
dualar.tekrar: Three times a day (morning and evening), before going to sleep
dualar.neZaman: In the morning, in the evening, before going to sleep, at any time
dualar.aciklama: Our mother Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her) narrated that every night before going to sleep, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would recite these two surahs, blow into his hands, and then wipe them over his body (Bukhari, Fedâilü'l-Kur'ân, 14).
dualar.not: It is recited especially for protection from unseen harm such as the evil eye and magic.

dualar.baslik: Surah an-Nas (Kul e'ûzü birabbinnâs)
dualar.arapca: قُلْ أَعُوذُ بِرَبِّ النَّاسِ ﴿١﴾ مَلِكِ النَّاسِ ﴿٢﴾ إِلَٰهِ النَّاسِ ﴿٣﴾ مِنْ شَرِّ الْوَسْوَاسِ الْخَنَّاسِ ﴿٤﴾ الَّذِي يُوَسْوِسُ فِي صُدُورِ النَّاسِ ﴿٥﴾ مِنَ الْجِنَّةِ وَالنَّاسِ
dualar.okunus: Kul e'ûzü birabbi'n-nâs. Meliki'n-nâs. İlâhi'n-nâs. Min şerri'l-vesvâsi'l-hannâs. Ellezi yüvesvisü fî sudûri'n-nâs. Mine'l-cinneti ve'n-nâs.
dualar.anlam: Say: I seek refuge in the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind, from the evil of the retreating whisperer who whispers into the hearts of mankind, whether from among jinn or humans.
dualar.kaynak: The Noble Qur'an (Elmalılı Hamdi Yazır translation)
dualar.tekrar: Three times a day (morning and evening), before going to sleep
dualar.neZaman: In the morning, in the evening, before going to sleep, at any time
dualar.aciklama: Surah an-Nas teaches us to seek refuge in Allah, especially from the evil of Satan, who puts whispers into hearts. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stated that nothing like these two surahs had been revealed in the Torah, the Gospel, or the Qur'an (Tirmidhi, Fedâilü'l-Kur'ân, 58).
dualar.not: Reciting Surahs al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, and an-Nas together is a practice followed for protection from the evil eye and harm, in accordance with the Sunnah of our Prophet.

dualar.baslik: The Supplication of Prophet Yunus (peace be upon him) (Zünnûn Duası)
dualar.arapca: لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
dualar.okunus: Lâ ilâhe illâ ente sübhâneke innî küntü mine'z-zâlimîn.
dualar.anlam: There is no deity but You. Glory be to You! Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.
dualar.kaynak: The Noble Qur'an, Surah al-Anbiya 87; Tirmidhi, Tefsîru'l-Kur'ân, 21/3244 (hasan-sahih)
dualar.tekrar: There is no limit on the number of times; it may be repeated as needed
dualar.neZaman: In times of sorrow, distress, and hardship
dualar.aciklama: When Prophet Yunus (peace be upon him) was in the belly of the fish, he called upon Allah with this supplication, and his supplication was answered. The narration in Tirmidhi states that this is one of the great supplications recited in times of distress.
dualar.not: It may be repeated often in times of sorrow and distress; the response comes from Allah.

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Protection from Whispers and Satan
dualar.arapca: وَقُلْ رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ هَمَزَاتِ الشَّيَاطِينِ ﴿٩٧﴾ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ رَبِّ أَنْ يَحْضُرُونِ
dualar.okunus: Ve kull rabbi e'ûzü bike min hemezâti'ş-şeyâtîn. Ve e'ûzü bike rabbi en yahdurûn.
dualar.anlam: And say: My Lord! I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils, and I seek refuge in You from their presence near me.
dualar.kaynak: The Noble Qur'an, Surah al-Mu'minun 97–98 (Elmalılı Hamdi Yazır translation)
dualar.tekrar: There is no numerical limit; recite as needed
dualar.neZaman: When experiencing intrusive whispers, to seek protection from Satan's incitements
dualar.aciklama: These verses teach us to seek refuge in Allah from the hidden whispers and incitements of devils.
dualar.not: These are among the powerful Quranic verses that teach us to seek refuge in Allah from intrusive whispers and Satan's incitements.

kategoriler.isim: Morning and Evening Remembrances for Protection

dualar.baslik: Prayer for Protection Recited Three Times
dualar.arapca: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الَّذِي لَا يَضُرُّ مَعَ اسْمِهِ شَيْءٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَلَا فِي السَّمَاءِ وَهُوَ السَّمِيعُ الْعَلِيمُ
dualar.okunus: Bismillâhillezî lâ yedurru mea'smihî şey'ün fi'l-ardı ve lâ fi's-semâi ve hüve's-semî'u'l-'alîm.
dualar.anlam: In the name of Allah; when His name is mentioned, nothing on earth or in heaven can cause harm. He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Adab, 101/5088; Tirmidhi, Da'awat, 20/3388; Ibn Majah, Du'a, 10/3869; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Three times each morning and evening
dualar.neZaman: In the morning and evening
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever recites this prayer three times in the morning or evening, nothing will harm them." (Abu Dawud, 4/322; Tirmidhi, 5/567).
dualar.not: Recited for general protection.

dualar.baslik: Prayer for Protection from the Evil of What He Has Created
dualar.arapca: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا خَلَقَ
dualar.okunus: Eûzü bi-kelimâtillâhi't-tâmmâti min şerri mâ halak.
dualar.anlam: I seek refuge in the perfect and complete words of Allah from the evil of everything He has created.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Dhikr, 53/2708; Tirmidhi, Da'awat, 15/3437; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Three times each morning and evening
dualar.neZaman: In the morning and evening; also when stopping to stay somewhere
dualar.aciklama: It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "If you had recited this prayer in the evening, nothing would have harmed you."
dualar.not: It is recommended to recite it in the morning and evening and when entering a new place.

dualar.baslik: The Master Prayer for Forgiveness
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ أَنْتَ رَبِّي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ خَلَقْتَنِي وَأَنَا عَبْدُكَ وَأَنَا عَلَى عَهْدِكَ وَوَعْدِكَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّ مَا صَنَعْتُ أَبُوءُ لَكَ بِنِعْمَتِكَ عَلَيَّ وَأَبُوءُ بِذَنْبِي فَاغْفِرْ لِي فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَغْفِرُ الذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme ente rabbî lâ ilâhe illâ ente halaktenî ve ene abdüke ve ene alâ ahdike ve va'dike mesteta'tü eûzü bike min şerri mâ sana'tü ebû'ü leke bi-ni'metike aleyye ve ebû'ü bi-zenbî fağfirlî fe-innehû lâ yağfirü'z-zünûbe illâ ent.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! You are my Lord; there is no true deity except You. You created me, and I am Your servant. I remain faithful to my promise and covenant with You as far as I am able. I seek refuge in You from the evil of what I have done. I acknowledge the blessings You have bestowed upon me, and I acknowledge my sin. Forgive me, for none forgives sins except You.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Da'awat, 2/6306; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Morning and evening
dualar.neZaman: In the morning and evening
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ described this prayer as "the master prayer for forgiveness" and said: "Whoever recites it during the day with conviction and dies before nightfall will be in Paradise."
dualar.not: It is the most comprehensive prayer for forgiveness.

dualar.baslik: The Most Virtuous Tasbih
dualar.arapca: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ
dualar.okunus: Sübhânallâhi ve bi-hamdihî.
dualar.anlam: I declare Allah free from all imperfections and praise Him.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Dhikr, 85/2691; Tirmidhi, Da'awat, 105/3466; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: 100 times (morning and evening)
dualar.neZaman: In the morning and evening
dualar.aciklama: "Whoever says sübhânallâhi ve bi-hamdihî one hundred times in a day will have all their sins forgiven, even if they are as much as the foam of the sea." (Muslim, Dhikr, 85).
dualar.not: It is a means of forgiveness of sins and spiritual protection.

dualar.baslik: Remembrance of Allah's Oneness
dualar.arapca: لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
dualar.okunus: Lâ ilâhe illallâhu vahdehû lâ şerîke leh, lehü'l-mülkü ve lehü'l-hamdü ve hüve alâ külli şey'in kadîr.
dualar.anlam: There is no true deity except Allah. He is One and has no partner. Dominion belongs to Him, and all praise is due to Him. He has power over all things.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Da'awat, 65; Muslim, Masajid, 150/594; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: 10 times in the morning and evening (or after each salah)
dualar.neZaman: In the morning and evening or after each obligatory salah
dualar.aciklama: It has been said that for the person who recites this remembrance in the morning and evening, "Allah records a reward equal to that of freeing a slave."
dualar.not: It is one of the most comprehensive expressions of Allah's oneness.

dualar.baslik: Remembrance of Trust in Allah
dualar.arapca: حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ
dualar.okunus: Hasbünallahü ve ni'me'l-vekîl.
dualar.anlam: Allah is sufficient for us. What an excellent disposer of affairs He is!
dualar.kaynak: The Quran, Surah Al 'Imran 173; Bukhari, Tafsir, 3; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Seven times in the morning and evening
dualar.neZaman: In the morning, evening, and at times of fear and anxiety
dualar.aciklama: Surah Al 'Imran, verse 173, states that the believers placed their trust in Allah with these words.
dualar.not: It is recommended to recite it in every situation involving fear, anxiety, or a need to place one's trust in Allah.

dualar.baslik: Prayer for Health and Well-Being
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ الْعَفْوَ وَالْعَافِيَةَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme innî es'elüke'l-afve ve'l-âfiyete fi'd-dünyâ ve'l-âhire.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! I ask You for forgiveness and well-being in this world and in the Hereafter.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Adab, 110/5074; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once in the morning and evening
dualar.neZaman: In the morning and evening
dualar.aciklama: This is the concise opening sentence of a more comprehensive prayer for well-being recited in the morning and evening. The narration in Abu Dawud reports that the Messenger of Allah did not neglect to ask for well-being in the morning and evening.
dualar.not: The longer wording also asks for well-being in religion, worldly life, family, and wealth. The short form may also be recited as a prayer.

dualar.baslik: Prayer for the Blessings of the Day
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ مَا أَصْبَحَ بِي مِنْ نِعْمَةٍ فَمِنْكَ وَحْدَكَ لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ فَلَكَ الْحَمْدُ وَلَكَ الشُّكْرُ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme mâ asbeha bî min ni'metin fe-minke vahdeke lâ şerîke lek, fe-leke'l-hamdü ve leke'ş-şükr.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! Every blessing I have this morning has come from You alone. You have no partner. All praise and thanks are Yours.
dualar.kaynak: Nasa'i, 'Amal al-Yawm wa'l-Laylah, 30; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.derece: A well-known morning and evening prayer of gratitude
dualar.tekrar: Once in the morning and evening
dualar.neZaman: In the morning and evening
dualar.aciklama: Through this prayer, a person acknowledges that the blessings they have are from Allah and turns to Him in praise and gratitude.
dualar.not: It is a prayer that renews one's awareness of gratitude.

dualar.baslik: Prayer of Submission to Allah at Bedtime
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ أَسْلَمْتُ نَفْسِي إِلَيْكَ وَوَجَّهْتُ وَجْهِي إِلَيْكَ وَفَوَّضْتُ أَمْرِي إِلَيْكَ وَأَلْجَأْتُ ظَهْرِي إِلَيْكَ رَغْبَةً وَرَهْبَةً إِلَيْكَ لَا مَلْجَأَ وَلَا مَنْجَا مِنْكَ إِلَّا إِلَيْكَ آمَنْتُ بِكِتَابِكَ الَّذِي أَنْزَلْتَ وَبِنَبِيِّكَ الَّذِي أَرْسَلْتَ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme eslemtü nefsî ileyke ve vecchehtü vechî ileyke ve fevvadtü emrî ileyke ve elce'tü zahrî ileyke ragabeten ve rahbeten ileyke, lâ melcee ve lâ mencâ minke illâ ileyke. Âmentü bi-kitâbike'llezî enzelte ve bi-nebiyyike'llezî erselte.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! I have submitted myself to You, turned my face toward You, entrusted my affairs to You, and rested my back upon You. I have turned to You with hope and fear. There is no refuge or escape from You except in You. I have believed in the Book You revealed and the prophet You sent.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Da'awat, 7/6313; Muslim, Dhikr, 56/2714; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once every night before going to bed
dualar.neZaman: Immediately before sleeping
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ stated that a person who recites this prayer and dies that night will have died upon the fitrah.
dualar.not: It is recited to be under Allah's protection throughout the night.

dualar.baslik: Prayer for Sleep and Waking
dualar.arapca: بِاسْمِكَ اللَّهُمَّ أَحْيَا وَأَمُوتُ
dualar.okunus: Bismike'llâhümme ahyâ ve emût.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! In Your name I die, and in Your name I live.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Da'awat, 10/6324; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once every night before going to bed
dualar.neZaman: Immediately before sleeping
dualar.aciklama: It is narrated from our mother Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) that whenever the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went to bed at night, he would recite Surahs al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, and an-Nas into his palms, then wipe his hands over his body. He would then recite this prayer.
dualar.not: One goes to sleep after the prayer "Bismike'llâhümme ahyâ ve emût".

dualar.baslik: Verses Recited for Protection at Night
dualar.arapca: (Ayetü'l-Kürsi ve Bakara 285-286)
dualar.okunus: (Ayetü'l-Kürsi ve Âmenerrasûlü ayetleri)
dualar.anlam: This entry is a reminder of Ayat al-Kursi and the Amanar-Rasul verses, which are recommended to be recited at night. Translations of these verses can be viewed in the relevant verse sections of the app.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Wakalah, 10; Muslim, Musafirin, 257
dualar.tekrar: Once every night before going to bed
dualar.neZaman: Immediately before sleeping
dualar.aciklama: It has been stated that whoever sleeps after reciting Ayat al-Kursi is protected by Allah, and that the two verses of al-Baqarah 285–286 suffice for the person who recites them at night.
dualar.not: They are recited at night for protection from dangers such as thieves, fire, and jinn.

dualar.baslik: Seeking Refuge in the Creator of the Heavens and the Earth
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ فَاطِرَ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ عَالِمَ الْغَيْبِ وَالشَّهَادَةِ رَبَّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَمَلِيكَهُ أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ فَأَجِرْنِي مِنَ النَّارِ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme fâtıra's-semâvâti ve'l-ard, âlime'l-ğaybi ve'ş-şehâdeti rabbe külli şey'in ve melîkeh, eşhedü en lâ ilâhe illâ ente fe-ehırnî mine'n-nâr.
dualar.anlam: O Allah, Creator of the heavens and the earth, Knower of the unseen and the seen, Lord and Owner of all things! I bear witness that there is no deity except You. Protect me from the fire of Hell.
dualar.kaynak: Tirmidhi, Da'awat, 9/3392; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once every night before going to bed
dualar.neZaman: Immediately before sleeping
dualar.aciklama: This is one of the comprehensive prayers recited before sleep with the intention of seeking refuge in Allah and protection from punishment in the Hereafter.
dualar.not: It is recited with the intention of seeking refuge in Allah from the punishment of the Hereafter and the evil of the self.

dualar.baslik: Muâvvizeteyn (Protective Surahs)
dualar.arapca: Kul hüvellâhü ehad, Kul e'ûzü birabbil felak, Kul e'ûzü birabbinnâs.
dualar.okunus: İhlas, Felak ve Nas sureleri.
dualar.anlam: This entry serves as a reminder to recite Surahs al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas with the intention of seeking protection. Translations of the surahs can be viewed on their respective screens in the app.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Fada'il al-Qur'an, 14; Tirmidhi, Da'awat, 22/3402; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Three times each before going to bed
dualar.neZaman: Immediately before going to sleep
dualar.aciklama: According to the narration of Aisha (may Allah be pleased with her), whenever the Prophet ﷺ went to bed at night, he would bring his hands together, recite Surahs al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq and an-Nas into his palms and blow into them, then wipe his hands over his body, starting with his head.
dualar.not: It is Sunnah to recite them when going to bed at night; by Allah's permission, they are a means of protection and peace.

kategoriler.isim: Protection from the Evil Eye, Envy and the Evil Gaze

dualar.baslik: Surahs for Protection from the Evil Eye
dualar.arapca: Felak ve Nas sureleri
dualar.okunus: (Yukarıda A kategorisinde verilmiştir)
dualar.anlam: This entry serves as a reminder of the surahs recited for protection from the evil eye. Translations of the relevant surahs are available in the surah sections of the app.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Tibb, 36; Muslim, Salam, 38/2188; Ibn Majah, Tibb, 31/3510; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Three, seven or more times as needed
dualar.neZaman: When the evil eye is suspected, or morning and evening for protection
dualar.aciklama: The Prophet ﷺ said, "The evil eye is real" (Bukhari, Tibb, 36), and recited these surahs to protect his grandsons Hasan and Husayn from the evil eye.
dualar.not: The evil eye is accepted in Islam as a reality that is part of divine decree.

dualar.baslik: Supplication to Be Recited by the Person Who Has Cast the Evil Eye
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ فِيهِ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme bârik fîh.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! Grant them blessings.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Tibb, 18/3892; Malik, Muwatta, 2/936; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once
dualar.neZaman: When someone looks at something they like and admire and fears that they may cause it harm
dualar.aciklama: "If one of you sees something they like in themselves or their brother, let them pray for blessings for it. For the evil eye is real." (Abu Dawud, Tibb, 18/3892).
dualar.not: The phrase "Mâşâallah, lâ kuvvete illâ billâh" may also be said in this context.

dualar.baslik: The "Eûzü bi-kelimâtillâhi't-tâmmât" Supplication
dualar.arapca: أَعُوذُ بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّاتِ مِنْ غَضَبِهِ وَعِقَابِهِ وَشَرِّ عِبَادِهِ وَمِنْ هَمَزَاتِ الشَّيَاطِينِ وَأَنْ يَحْضُرُونِ
dualar.okunus: Eûzü bi-kelimâtillâhi't-tâmmâti min gadabihî ve ikâbihî ve şerri ibâdihî ve min hemezâti'ş-şeyâtîni ve en yahdurûn.
dualar.anlam: I seek refuge in the complete and perfect words of Allah from Allah's anger and punishment, the evil of His servants, the promptings of the devils and their coming near me.
dualar.kaynak: Tirmidhi, Da'awat, 15/3437; Abu Dawud, Adab, 101/5088; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Three times each morning and evening
dualar.neZaman: For protection from the evil eye and similar harms
dualar.aciklama: It is one of the most comprehensive supplications for protection from all kinds of visible and invisible evil, such as the evil eye, envy, magic and jinn.
dualar.not: It is recited especially for protection from the evil of an envious person.

dualar.baslik: Healing with al-Fatihah, Protection with Ayat al-Kursi
dualar.arapca: Fatiha suresi ve Ayetü'l-Kürsi
dualar.okunus: Bu bölümde Fâtiha sûresi ve Âyetü'l-Kürsî okunur.
dualar.anlam: This entry serves as a reminder to recite Surah al-Fatihah with the intention of seeking healing and Ayat al-Kursi with the intention of seeking protection. Translations of the relevant texts can be viewed on the surah and verse screens in the app.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Tibb, 19/3900 (reciting al-Fatihah in ruqyah); Bukhari, Wakala, 10 (on protection at night through Ayat al-Kursi)
dualar.derece: Sahih (general narrations on healing and protection)
dualar.tekrar: As needed
dualar.neZaman: When one wishes to recite them with the intention of seeking healing and protection
dualar.aciklama: In a sahih hadith, al-Fatihah was recited as a means of ruqyah and healing. Ayat al-Kursi is also well known for its virtue in providing protection. Reciting these two texts with the intention of seeking general protection and healing, including when the evil eye is suspected, is a common practice.
dualar.not: No sahih hadith is cited that directly says, 'Recite these two together against the evil eye'; the basis here is their general virtue for healing and protection established by sahih narrations.

dualar.baslik: Verses to Be Recited Against Envy
dualar.arapca: Bakara Suresi 102. ayet, Felak suresi 5. ayet, Kalem Suresi 51-52. ayetler
dualar.okunus: Bu bölümde adı geçen ayetler okunur.
dualar.anlam: A translation of the Quran should be consulted for the meaning of these verses.
dualar.kaynak: The Quran; Tirmidhi, Tafsir, 68/3310 (hasan-sahih)
dualar.tekrar: As needed
dualar.neZaman: For protection from the harm of an envious person
dualar.aciklama: Verses 51–52 of Surah al-Qalam are among the verses recommended for recitation against the evil eye of those who envy.
dualar.not: Envy is a disease of the heart; seeking refuge in Allah and reciting these verses for protection is Sunnah.

kategoriler.isim: Protection from Satan and Intrusive Thoughts

dualar.baslik: Verses for Protection from the Promptings of Devils
dualar.arapca: وَقُلْ رَبِّ أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ هَمَزَاتِ الشَّيَاطِينِ ﴿٩٧﴾ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ رَبِّ أَنْ يَحْضُرُونِ
dualar.okunus: Ve kull rabbi e'ûzü bike min hemezâti'ş-şeyâtîn. Ve e'ûzü bike rabbi en yahdurûn.
dualar.anlam: My Lord! I seek refuge in You from the incitements of the devils. I also seek refuge in You from their presence near me.
dualar.kaynak: The Quran, Surah al-Mu'minun 97–98
dualar.tekrar: There is no set limit on the number of times
dualar.neZaman: When intrusive thoughts arise or one feels Satan's incitements
dualar.aciklama: These two verses teach one to seek refuge in Allah from the intrusive thoughts Satan casts into a person's heart.
dualar.not: Intrusive thoughts are Satan's most basic weapon.

dualar.baslik: Reciting the Eûzü and Besmele
dualar.arapca: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ - بِسْمِ اللَّهِ الرَّحْمَٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ
dualar.okunus: Eûzü billâhi mine'ş-şeytâni'r-racîm. Bismillâhi'r-rahmâni'r-rahîm.
dualar.anlam: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan. In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Tafsir, 16/1; Muslim, Salat, 41/548; Abu Dawud, Salat, 46/775
dualar.tekrar: Before beginning to read the Quran, before beginning salah, and when experiencing intrusive thoughts
dualar.neZaman: When beginning to read the Quran, leaving home, beginning to eat, and when experiencing intrusive thoughts
dualar.aciklama: Allah Most High has commanded seeking refuge in Allah from Satan before beginning to read the Quran (an-Nahl 16/98).
dualar.not: Reciting "Eûzü" when intrusive thoughts arise is the most basic Sunnah practice for breaking Satan's influence.

dualar.baslik: Verses and Surahs Recited for Protection from Satan
dualar.arapca: Ayetü'l-Kürsi, İhlas, Felak, Nas sureleri
dualar.okunus: (İlgili ayet ve surelerin okunuşu)
dualar.anlam: This entry brings together reminders of the verses and surahs recited for protection from Satan. Translations of the relevant texts can be viewed in the surah and verse sections of the app.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Wakala, 10; Muslim, Salat, 222/813
dualar.derece: Sahih (the virtues of the relevant verses and surahs are established)
dualar.tekrar: After every salah, morning and evening, and before bed
dualar.neZaman: Regularly, for protection from Satan's intrusive thoughts
dualar.aciklama: Hadith establishes that reciting Ayat al-Kursi at night is a means of protection from Satan.
dualar.not: Surahs al-Falaq and an-Nas also teach seeking refuge in Allah from intrusive thoughts and visible and invisible evils.

dualar.baslik: What to Do When Intrusive Thoughts Arise
dualar.arapca: قُلْ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَحَدٌ (İhlas suresi)
dualar.okunus: Kul hüvellâhü ehad.
dualar.anlam: This entry serves as a reminder to recite Surah al-Ikhlas when intrusive thoughts arise. A translation of the surah can be viewed on its corresponding screen in the app.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Salat, 223/2203; Ibn Majah, Adab, 52/3774
dualar.tekrar: Three times when intrusive thoughts arise
dualar.neZaman: When Satan's intrusive thoughts arise during salah or worship
dualar.aciklama: The Prophet ﷺ said: "When it comes, spit to your right three times and say 'Eûzü billâhi mine'ş-şeytâni'r-racîm'."
dualar.not: This practice is performed only when experiencing intrusive thoughts.

dualar.baslik: The Essence of Seeking Refuge in Allah
dualar.arapca: حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ
dualar.okunus: Hasbünallahü ve ni'me'l-vekîl.
dualar.anlam: Allah is sufficient for us. What an excellent trustee He is!
dualar.kaynak: The Quran, Aal Imran 173; Bukhari, Tafsir, 3
dualar.tekrar: There is no set limit on the number of times
dualar.neZaman: In moments of any kind of intrusive thoughts, fear or doubt
dualar.aciklama: The phrase 'Hasbünallahü ve ni'me'l-vekîl' is a great form of dhikr that expresses reliance on Allah in times of difficulty and fear.
dualar.not: It is an expression of submission that gives the heart confidence in moments of intrusive thoughts, fear and anxiety.

dualar.baslik: The Supplication of Musa (peace be upon him)
dualar.arapca: رَبِّ إِنِّي لِمَا أَنْزَلْتَ إِلَيَّ مِنْ خَيْرٍ فَقِيرٌ
dualar.okunus: Rabbi innî limâ enzelte ileyye min hayrin fakîr.
dualar.anlam: My Lord! Indeed, I am in need of whatever good You send down to me.
dualar.kaynak: The Quran, Surah al-Qasas 24
dualar.tekrar: As needed
dualar.neZaman: At times when intrusive thoughts intensify and one feels helpless and powerless
dualar.aciklama: Prophet Musa (peace be upon him) made this supplication when he left Egypt and reached Madyan.
dualar.not: When facing intrusive thoughts, it is important to acknowledge one's need for Allah.

kategoriler.isim: Supplications for Fear, Distress, Grief and Debt

dualar.baslik: The Supplication for Distress Narrated by Anas ibn Malik
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ رَحْمَتَكَ أَرْجُو فَلَا تَكِلْنِي إِلَى نَفْسِي طَرْفَةَ عَيْنٍ وَأَصْلِحْ لِي شَأْنِي كُلَّهُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme rahmeteke ercû fe-lâ tekilnî ilâ nefsî tarfete aynin ve aslih lî şe'nî külleh, lâ ilâhe illâ ent.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! I hope for Your mercy. Do not leave me to myself even for the blink of an eye. Set all my affairs right for me. There is no true god but You.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Adab, 110/5087; Tirmidhi, Da'awat, 78/3524 (hasan-sahih); Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: May be repeated as needed
dualar.neZaman: At times of fear, anxiety, distress and sadness
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ often recited this supplication.
dualar.not: It is among the most comprehensive supplications recommended at times of fear and distress.

dualar.baslik: The Supplication the Prophet Recited When Grieved
dualar.arapca: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْعَظِيمُ الْحَلِيمُ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَرَبُّ الْأَرْضِ رَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْكَرِيمِ
dualar.okunus: Lâ ilâhe illallâhu'l-azîmü'l-halîm, lâ ilâhe illallâhu rabbü'l-arşi'l-azîm, lâ ilâhe illallâhu rabbü's-semâvâti ve rabbü'l-ardı rabbü'l-arşi'l-kerîm.
dualar.anlam: There is no true god but Allah, the Most Great, the Forbearing. There is no true god but Allah, Lord of the Mighty Throne. There is no true god but Allah, Lord of the heavens, Lord of the earth and Lord of the Noble Throne.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Da'awat, 42/6346; Muslim, Dhikr, 43/2730; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: At times of grief and sadness
dualar.neZaman: At times of grief and sadness
dualar.aciklama: It is narrated from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this supplication whenever he felt grief and sadness.
dualar.not: This supplication centers on tawhid; it eases distress by reminding one of Allah's greatness.

dualar.baslik: The Supplication of Abu Umamah
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْهَمِّ وَالْحَزَنِ وَالْعَجْزِ وَالْكَسَلِ وَالْجُبْنِ وَالْبُخْلِ وَضَلَعِ الدَّيْنِ وَغَلَبَةِ الرِّجَالِ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme innî eûzü bike mine'l-hemmi ve'l-hazeni ve'l-aczi ve'l-keseli ve'l-cübnî ve'l-buhli ve dala'i'd-deyni ve galebeti'r-rical.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! I seek refuge in You from anxiety and sadness, from helplessness and laziness, from cowardice and miserliness, from being overwhelmed by debt and from the oppression of people.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Salah, 367/1541; Tirmidhi, Da'awat, 72/3511; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: May be recited morning and evening
dualar.neZaman: At times of debt and distress; regularly in the morning and evening
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ frequently made these supplications.
dualar.not: Debt is a serious responsibility in Islam, and this supplication is recited to seek relief from it.

dualar.baslik: Surah al-Anbiya, Verse 87 (The Supplication of Dhun-Nun)
dualar.arapca: لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
dualar.okunus: Lâ ilâhe illâ ente sübhâneke innî küntü mine'z-zâlimîn.
dualar.anlam: There is no god but You. Glory be to You! Indeed, I was among the wrongdoers.
dualar.kaynak: The Quran, al-Anbiya 87; Tirmidhi, Tafsir al-Quran, 21/3244 (hasan-sahih)
dualar.derece: Quran (the hadith narration is graded hasan-sahih)
dualar.tekrar: There is no limit on the number of repetitions
dualar.neZaman: At times of any kind of distress, hardship, grief, debt, imprisonment or illness
dualar.aciklama: This verse is the supplication of Prophet Yunus. The narration in Tirmidhi identifies it as one of the great supplications recited in times of distress.
dualar.not: It may be repeated often during difficult times; the answer comes from Allah.

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Happiness in This World and the Hereafter
dualar.arapca: رَبَّنَا آتِنَا فِي الدُّنْيَا حَسَنَةً وَفِي الْآخِرَةِ حَسَنَةً وَقِنَا عَذَابَ النَّارِ
dualar.okunus: Rabbenâ âtinâ fi'd-dünyâ haseneten ve fi'l-âhirati haseneten ve kınâ azâbe'n-nâr.
dualar.anlam: Our Lord! Grant us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire!
dualar.kaynak: The Quran, Surah al-Baqarah 201
dualar.tekrar: After every salah, at any time
dualar.neZaman: At any time, especially during times of distress
dualar.aciklama: It is one of the most comprehensive supplications, encompassing every kind of good in this world and the Hereafter.
dualar.not: It is one of the most frequently recited Quranic supplications.

dualar.baslik: Prophet Ibrahim's (peace be upon him) Supplication for Forgiveness
dualar.arapca: رَبَّنَا اغْفِرْ لِي وَلِوَالِدَيَّ وَلِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ يَوْمَ يَقُومُ الْحِسَابُ
dualar.okunus: Rabbenâ'ğfir lî ve li-vâlideyye ve lil-mü'minîne yevme yekûmu'l-hisâb.
dualar.anlam: Our Lord! Forgive me, my parents and the believers on the Day when everyone is called to account.
dualar.kaynak: The Quran, Surah Ibrahim 41
dualar.tekrar: After every salah, at any time
dualar.neZaman: At any time, especially during the final sitting of salah
dualar.aciklama: It is the most well-known supplication of Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him).
dualar.not: Praying for one's parents and other believers alongside oneself is an act of spiritual solidarity.

dualar.baslik: Overcoming Fear with Remembrance of Reliance on Allah
dualar.arapca: حَسْبُنَا اللَّهُ وَنِعْمَ الْوَكِيلُ
dualar.okunus: Hasbünallahü ve ni'me'l-vekîl.
dualar.anlam: Allah is sufficient for us. What an excellent Trustee He is!
dualar.kaynak: The Quran, Al Imran 173; Bukhari, Tafsir, 3
dualar.tekrar: As needed
dualar.neZaman: At times of fear, anxiety, grief, distress and difficulty
dualar.aciklama: This remembrance is a powerful expression of reliance on Allah at times of fear, anxiety and distress.
dualar.not: Repeating this remembrance in times of fear can bring peace and reassurance to the heart.

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Leaving the Home
dualar.arapca: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ عَلَى اللَّهِ لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ
dualar.okunus: Bismillâhi tevekkeltü alâllâhi lâ havle ve lâ kuvvete illâ billâh.
dualar.anlam: I leave in the name of Allah; I place my trust in Allah. There is no power or strength except through Allah's help.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Adab, 101/5095; Tirmidhi, Da'awat, 12/3426 (hasan-sahih); Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once each time one leaves home
dualar.neZaman: When leaving home
dualar.aciklama: "Whoever says this supplication when leaving home will be told, 'This is sufficient for you; you are protected,' and Satan will move away from them." (Abu Dawud, 5095).
dualar.not: Reciting this supplication when leaving home is a means of protection from all kinds of accidents and misfortunes throughout the day.

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Entering the Home
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَ الْمَوْلَجِ وَخَيْرَ الْمَخْرَجِ بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَلَجْنَا وَبِسْمِ اللَّهِ خَرَجْنَا وَعَلَى اللَّهِ رَبِّنَا تَوَكَّلْنَا
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme innî es'elüke hayre'l-mevleci ve hayre'l-mahreci. Bismillâhi velecna ve bismillâhi haracnâ ve alâllâhi rabbinâ tevekkelnâ.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! I ask You to make both my entering and my leaving blessed. In the name of Allah we enter, and in the name of Allah we leave. We place our trust in Allah, our Lord.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Adab, 102/5096; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once each time one enters the home
dualar.neZaman: When entering the home
dualar.aciklama: It is narrated from Jabir ibn Abdillah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this supplication when entering the home.
dualar.not: When entering the home, it is Sunnah to enter with the right foot, say "Bismillâhi" and greet the household.

dualar.baslik: Greeting the Household When Entering
dualar.arapca: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ
dualar.okunus: Es-selâmü aleyküm ve rahmetullâhi ve berakâtüh.
dualar.anlam: Peace, Allah's mercy and His blessings be upon you.
dualar.kaynak: Surah al-An'am 54; Surah an-Nur 61; Tirmidhi, Isti'dhan, 10/2699 (hasan)
dualar.tekrar: Each time one enters the home
dualar.neZaman: Greeting the household when entering the home
dualar.aciklama: "My child, when you enter upon your family, greet them with salam. This will be a blessing for you and your household." (Tirmidhi, Isti'dhan, 10).
dualar.not: It is recommended to give salam when entering the home, even if no one is inside.

dualar.baslik: Protection at Home Through the Quran and Remembrance
dualar.arapca: Bakara suresi ve Ayetü'l-Kürsi
dualar.okunus: Bu bölümde Bakara sûresi ve Âyetü'l-Kürsî gibi ilgili metinler okunur.
dualar.anlam: This entry serves as a reminder of the intention to seek protection through recitation of the Quran and remembrance at home. Translations of the relevant verses and surahs can be found in their respective sections in the app.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Musafirin, 212/780 (Satan does not enter a home in which Surah al-Baqarah is recited); Bukhari, Wakalah, 10 (on the protection provided by Ayat al-Kursi at night)
dualar.tekrar: Regularly
dualar.neZaman: With the intention of seeking protection and blessings at home, especially at night and when the Quran is recited at home
dualar.aciklama: A sahih hadith states that Satan will stay away from a home in which Surah al-Baqarah is recited. Ayat al-Kursi is also well known as a verse of protection. For this reason, maintaining spiritual vitality at home through the Quran and remembrance is recommended.
dualar.not: There is no single established sahih wording that specifically instructs one to recite these verses when entering the home; this entry summarizes the practice of bringing blessings into the home through the Quran and remembrance.

dualar.baslik: Toilet Etiquette and Supplications
dualar.arapca: (Giriş) اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنَ الْخُبْثِ وَالْخَبَائِثِ - (Çıkış) غُفْرَانَكَ
dualar.okunus: (Giriş) Allâhümme innî eûzü bike mine'l-hubsi ve'l-habâis. - (Çıkış) Ğufrâneke.
dualar.anlam: When entering: O Allah! I seek refuge in You from male and female devils. When leaving: I seek Your forgiveness.
dualar.kaynak: (Entering) Bukhari, Wudu, 9/142; Muslim, Hayd, 17/375; (Leaving) Abu Dawud, Taharah, 20/30; Tirmidhi, Taharah, 14/7 (hasan)
dualar.tekrar: Each time one enters or leaves the toilet
dualar.neZaman: When entering and leaving the toilet
dualar.aciklama: This supplication is recited before entering the toilet, and one enters with the left foot; when leaving, one says "Ğufrâneke" and exits with the right foot.
dualar.not: Because the toilet is a place where devils are present, seeking protection with these supplications is Sunnah.

dualar.baslik: Supplication When Beginning a Journey
dualar.arapca: سُبْحَانَ الَّذِي سَخَّرَ لَنَا هَٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لَهُ مُقْرِنِينَ وَإِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا لَمُنْقَلِبُونَ
dualar.okunus: Sübhânellezî sehhara lenâ hâzâ ve mâ künnâ lehû mukrinîn. Ve innâ ilâ rabbinâ le-münkalibûn.
dualar.anlam: Glory be to Allah, who has placed these at our service; otherwise, we could not have mastered them. Indeed, we will return to our Lord.
dualar.kaynak: Qur'an, Surah az-Zukhruf 13-14; Abu Dawud, Jihad, 81/2602; Tirmidhi, Tafsir, 43/3246 (hasan-sahih); Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once whenever setting out on a journey
dualar.neZaman: When setting out on a journey and mounting a means of transport
dualar.aciklama: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ set out on a journey and mounted his means of transport, he would recite these verses and then say "Elhamdülillâh".
dualar.not: One should remember Allah and praise Him during a journey.

dualar.baslik: Supplication During a Journey
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّا نَسْأَلُكَ فِي سَفَرِنَا هَٰذَا الْبِرَّ وَالتَّقْوَىٰ وَمِنَ الْعَمَلِ مَا تَرْضَىٰ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme innâ nes'elüke fî seferinâ hâze'l-birra ve't-takvâ ve mine'l-ameli mâ terdâ.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! On this journey of ours, we ask You for goodness, taqwa, and deeds that please You.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Hajj, 415/1342; Abu Dawud, Jihad, 79/2596; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once during a journey
dualar.neZaman: When setting out on a journey
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would recite this supplication when setting out on a journey.
dualar.not: It is Sunnah to engage in remembrance and supplication at every stage of a journey.

dualar.baslik: Supplication a Traveling Companion Can Say for a Traveler
dualar.arapca: أَسْتَوْدِعُ اللَّهَ دِينَكَ وَأَمَانَتَكَ وَخَوَاتِيمَ عَمَلِكَ
dualar.okunus: Estevdi'ullâhe dîneke ve emâneteke ve havâtîme amelik.
dualar.anlam: I entrust your religion, what has been entrusted to you, and the end of your deeds to Allah.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Jihad, 80/2600; Tirmidhi, Supplications, 12/3445; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once when bidding farewell to a traveler
dualar.neZaman: When seeing a traveler off
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would recite this supplication when bidding farewell to a traveler.
dualar.not: With this supplication, one asks for the protection of the traveler's religion, property, and life.

dualar.baslik: Supplication on Returning from a Journey
dualar.arapca: آيِبُونَ تَائِبُونَ عَابِدُونَ لِرَبِّنَا حَامِدُونَ
dualar.okunus: Âibûne tâibûne âbidûne li-rabbinâ hâmidûn.
dualar.anlam: We return turning to our Lord, repenting, worshipping Him, and praising Him.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Jihad, 155/3085; Muslim, Hajj, 424/1348; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once when returning from a journey
dualar.neZaman: When returning from a journey and approaching one's hometown
dualar.aciklama: It is narrated from Ibn Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would recite this supplication when returning from a journey.
dualar.not: One should thank Allah upon returning from a journey.

kategoriler.isim: Supplications for the Protection of Children

dualar.baslik: Supplication to Protect Children from the Evil Eye and Illnesses
dualar.arapca: أُعِيذُكُمَا بِكَلِمَاتِ اللَّهِ التَّامَّةِ مِنْ كُلِّ شَيْطَانٍ وَهَامَّةٍ وَمِنْ كُلِّ عَيْنٍ لَامَّةٍ
dualar.okunus: U'îzükümâ bi-kelimâtillâhi't-tâmmeti min külli şeytânin ve hâmmetin ve min külli aynin lâmmetin.
dualar.anlam: I seek refuge for both of you in the perfect and complete words of Allah from the evil of every devil, every harmful creature, and every evil eye.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Prophets, 10/3190; Tirmidhi, Medicine, 16/2060 (hasan-sahih); Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Regularly every day (especially in the morning and evening)
dualar.neZaman: For the protection of children, whether they are asleep or awake
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would protect his grandsons Hasan and Husayn from the evil eye with this supplication.
dualar.not: Reciting a supplication for the protection of children is among the practices of authentic ruqyah.

dualar.baslik: Protecting Children with Surahs al-Falaq and an-Nas
dualar.arapca: Felak ve Nas sureleri
dualar.okunus: Bu bölümde Felak ve Nâs sûreleri okunur.
dualar.anlam: This entry is a reminder to recite Surahs al-Falaq and an-Nas for children. Translations of the surahs are available on their respective screens in the app.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Peace, 38/2188; Tirmidhi, Supplications, 22/3402
dualar.derece: Sahih (the protective virtue of the surahs)
dualar.tekrar: Three times a day (in the morning, evening, and before sleep)
dualar.neZaman: For the protection of children
dualar.aciklama: Surahs al-Falaq and an-Nas are surahs of seeking refuge in Allah. Reciting them over children is also considered to fall within the general framework of authentic ruqyah practices.
dualar.not: The essential thing is to seek refuge in Allah by reciting these surahs; the number of recitations and details of the practice should not be regarded as a mandatory formula.

dualar.baslik: Reciting Ayat al-Kursi at Night
dualar.arapca: Ayetü'l-Kürsi (Bakara 255)
dualar.okunus: Bu bölümde gece Âyetü'l-Kürsî okunur.
dualar.anlam: This entry is a reminder to recite Ayat al-Kursi at night. A translation of the verse can be viewed on the relevant verse screen in the app.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Agency, 10; Nasa'i, Actions of the Day, 100
dualar.derece: Sahih (the virtue of reciting it at night)
dualar.tekrar: Once every night before sleep
dualar.neZaman: At night before sleep; for oneself or while one's child is sleeping
dualar.aciklama: An authentic hadith states that a guardian will be appointed until morning for a person who recites Ayat al-Kursi at night, and Satan will not be able to approach them. Reciting this verse in the presence of children is also a common practice for protection.
dualar.not: No separate narration with wording specifically for a child is cited; the established virtue of the verse at night is the basis here.

dualar.baslik: Saying Bismillah Before Eating
dualar.arapca: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ
dualar.okunus: Bismillâh.
dualar.anlam: In the name of Allah.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Food 2-3; Muslim, Drinks 108; Tirmidhi, Food 47; Ibn Majah, Food 8
dualar.tekrar: Once before every meal and drink
dualar.neZaman: Immediately before beginning to eat or drink
dualar.aciklama: It is narrated from Umar ibn Abi Salamah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Say Bismillah, eat with your right hand, and eat from what is in front of you." (Bukhari, Food 2-3; Muslim, Drinks 108). In an authentic narration from Jabir (may Allah be pleased with him), the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a person says Bismillah when entering the house and eating, Satan says to his companions, 'You have neither a place to spend the night nor food to eat here.'" (Muslim, Drinks 103; Abu Dawud, Food 15; Ibn Majah, Supplication 19).
dualar.not: A person who forgets to say Bismillah at the beginning of a meal should say "Bismillâhi fî evvelih ve âhirih" (In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end) as soon as they remember. (Tirmidhi, Food 47; Abu Dawud, Food 15)

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Someone Who Forgot to Say Bismillah
dualar.arapca: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ فِي أَوَّلِهِ وَآخِرِهِ
dualar.okunus: Bismillâhi fî evvelih ve âhirih.
dualar.anlam: In the name of Allah at its beginning and its end.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Food 15; Tirmidhi, Food 47
dualar.tekrar: Once upon remembering during a meal that one forgot to say Bismillah
dualar.neZaman: As soon as one realizes while eating that one forgot to say Bismillah
dualar.aciklama: It is narrated from our mother Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you eats, let them say Bismillah. If they forget to say Bismillah at the beginning, let them say 'Bismillâhi fî evvelih ve âhirih' as soon as they remember." (Abu Dawud, Food 15; Tirmidhi, Food 47).
dualar.not: It is recommended to teach this supplication to children as well, because it is easy to remember and put into practice.

dualar.baslik: Supplication of Praise After Eating (Short)
dualar.arapca: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنَا وَسَقَانَا وَجَعَلَنَا مُسْلِمِينَ
dualar.okunus: Elhamdü lillâhillezî et'amenâ ve sekânâ ve ce'alenâ müslimîn.
dualar.anlam: Praise be to Allah who fed us, gave us drink, and made us Muslims.
dualar.kaynak: Tirmidhi, Supplications 55/3457; Abu Dawud, Food 52/3850; Ibn Majah, Food 16/3283; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once after every meal and drink
dualar.neZaman: Immediately after eating or drinking
dualar.aciklama: It is narrated from Anas ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah Most High is pleased with His servant who praises Him after eating or drinking." (Muslim, Remembrance 89; Tirmidhi, Food 18). This short supplication is one of the most authentic wordings for this practice of praise.
dualar.not: It is Sunnah to always praise Allah after eating and drinking; this supplication is its shortest and most common form.

dualar.baslik: Supplication of Praise After Eating (Comprehensive — Narration of Abu Umamah)
dualar.arapca: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ حَمْدًا كَثِيرًا طَيِّبًا مُبَارَكًا فِيهِ غَيْرَ مَكْفِيٍّ وَلَا مُوَدَّعٍ وَلَا مُسْتَغْنًى عَنْهُ رَبَّنَا
dualar.okunus: Elhamdü lillâhi hamden kesîran tayyiben mübâreken fîh, ğayra mekfiyyin ve lâ müvedde'ın ve lâ müsteğnen anhü Rabbenâ.
dualar.anlam: O our Lord! We praise You with countless praises, offered with pure feelings, increasing rather than diminishing, and accepted rather than turned away from Your presence.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Food 54; Abu Dawud, Food 52/3849; Ibn Majah, Food 16/3284; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once after every meal (instead of or in addition to the short supplication)
dualar.neZaman: Immediately after eating
dualar.aciklama: Narrated from Abu Umamah (may Allah be pleased with him): the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would recite this praise when rising from the meal. (Bukhari, At'imah 54). This supplication not only expresses gratitude but also acknowledges that Allah's blessings are inexhaustible and indispensable.
dualar.not: It can be recited alongside the short supplication; if the short supplication is sufficient, this one may be chosen as an addition.

dualar.baslik: Supplication of Gratitude for Provision
dualar.arapca: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَطْعَمَنِي هَٰذَا الطَّعَامَ وَرَزَقَنِيهِ مِنْ غَيْرِ حَوْلٍ مِنِّي وَلَا قُوَّةٍ
dualar.okunus: Elhamdü lillâhillezî et'amenî hâze't-ta'âme ve razakanîhi min ğayri havlin minnî ve lâ kuvveh.
dualar.anlam: Praise be to Allah, who fed me this food and provided it for me without any power or strength on my part.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Libas 1/4023; Tirmidhi, Da'awat 55/3458; Ibn Majah, At'imah 16/3285; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once after eating
dualar.neZaman: Immediately after eating
dualar.aciklama: This supplication clearly expresses that provision comes from Allah and that a servant cannot obtain it through their own power. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would recite this supplication after eating.
dualar.not: Tirmidhi's narration states that "the past sins of the person who recites this supplication will be forgiven." (Tirmidhi, Da'awat 55/3458)

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Blessings for One Who Offers Food
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ بَارِكْ لَهُمْ فِيمَا رَزَقْتَهُمْ وَاغْفِرْ لَهُمْ وَارْحَمْهُمْ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme bârik lehüm fîmâ razakdehüm vağfir lehüm verhemhüm.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! Bless the provision You have given them, forgive them, and have mercy on them.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Nikah 96/1427; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once after every meal eaten as a guest
dualar.neZaman: When supplicating for the host after eating at someone's home
dualar.aciklama: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ate at someone's home, he would make this supplication for the host. (Muslim, Nikah 96/1427).
dualar.not: It is Sunnah to make this supplication for the host after a meal eaten as a guest in their home.

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Healing When Visiting the Sick
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ النَّاسِ أَذْهِبِ الْبَأْسَ اشْفِ أَنْتَ الشَّافِي لَا شِفَاءَ إِلَّا شِفَاؤُكَ شِفَاءً لَا يُغَادِرُ سَقَمًا
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme rabbe'n-nâsi ezhibi'l-be'se'şfi ente'ş-şâfî lâ şifâe illâ şifâuke şifâen lâ yüğâdiru sekamâ.
dualar.anlam: O Allah, Lord of mankind! Remove the affliction and grant healing. You alone are the Healer. There is no healing except Your healing. Grant healing that leaves no trace of illness.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Marda 20, 38, 40; Muslim, Salam 46-49; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once when visiting the sick (or it may be repeated as needed)
dualar.neZaman: When visiting a sick person; recited at their bedside
dualar.aciklama: Narrated from our mother Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her): when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited sick members of his family, he would wipe the sick person with his right hand and recite this supplication. (Bukhari, Marda 20; Muslim, Salam 46). This supplication clearly acknowledges that healing comes only from Allah.
dualar.not: A sick person may also recite this supplication for themselves; adjusting the address in the "ezhibi'l-be'se" part with "aşfi" is in accordance with the Sunnah.

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Healing Recited Seven Times
dualar.arapca: أَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ الْعَظِيمَ رَبَّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ أَنْ يَشْفِيَكَ
dualar.okunus: Es'elüllâhe'l-azîme rabbe'l-arşi'l-azîmi en yeşfiyeke.
dualar.anlam: I ask Allah the Almighty, Lord of the Mighty Throne, to heal you.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Jana'iz 12/3106; Tirmidhi, Tibb 32/2084 (hasan-sahih); Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Seven times when visiting the sick
dualar.neZaman: When visiting a sick person whose death is not near
dualar.aciklama: Narrated from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him): the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If someone visits a sick person whose death is not near and says seven times in their presence, 'Es'elüllâhe'l-azîme rabbe'l-arşi'l-azîmi en yeşfiyeke,' Allah will heal that sick person." (Abu Dawud, Jana'iz 12/3106; Tirmidhi, Tibb 32/2084).
dualar.not: The phrase "whose death is not near" shows that it is appropriate to pray for any sick person whose time of death has not arrived.

dualar.baslik: Ruqyah Supplication for a Sick Person to Recite for Themselves
dualar.arapca: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ تُرْبَةُ أَرْضِنَا وَرِيقَةُ بَعْضِنَا يُشْفَى سَقِيمُنَا بِإِذْنِ رَبِّنَا
dualar.okunus: Bismillâhi türbetü ardınâ ve rîkatü ba'dınâ yüşfâ sakîmunâ bi-izni rabbinâ.
dualar.anlam: In the name of Allah; with the dust of our land and the saliva of some of us, our sick person is healed by the permission of our Lord.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Tibb 38/5746; Muslim, Salam 50/2194; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Recited when discomfort or pain is felt, while pressing a finger on the painful area
dualar.neZaman: When pain or discomfort is felt anywhere in the body
dualar.aciklama: Narrated from our mother Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her): the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would touch the ground with the index finger of his right hand at the painful area and recite this supplication. (Bukhari, Tibb 38/5746; Muslim, Salam 50/2194). This practice is an expression of pure reliance on Allah and seeking refuge in Him.
dualar.not: The phrase "the dust of our land" in this supplication is not understood to refer exclusively to the soil of Madinah; it is a Sunnah practice that can be performed anywhere.

dualar.baslik: Words of Comfort and Supplication When Visiting the Sick
dualar.arapca: لَا بَأْسَ طَهُورٌ إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ
dualar.okunus: Lâ be'se tahûrun inşâallâh.
dualar.anlam: There is no harm; if Allah wills, this will be a means of purification.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Tawhid 31/7470; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once when visiting the sick
dualar.neZaman: To comfort a sick person when visiting them
dualar.aciklama: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ visited a sick person, he would comfort them with these words: "It is nothing; if Allah wills, this illness will be an expiation for your sins." (Bukhari, Tawhid 31/7470). These words remind us that illness is a hardship and also a means of spiritual purification.
dualar.not: When saying these words, adopting a sincere, heartfelt, and compassionate manner is more in keeping with the Sunnah.

dualar.baslik: Comprehensive Supplication for Comfort and Healing When Visiting the Sick
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ اشْفِ عَبْدَكَ يَنْكَأُ لَكَ عَدُوًّا أَوْ يَمْشِي لَكَ إِلَى صَلَاةٍ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme'şfi abdeke yenke'ü leke adüvven ev yemşî leke ilâ salâh.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! Heal Your servant, so that they may either fight the enemy in Your cause or walk to salah seeking Your pleasure.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Jana'iz 11/3107; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once when visiting the sick
dualar.neZaman: When asking for healing for a sick person
dualar.aciklama: This supplication presents a distinctive theological framework that connects the request for healing with the motivation to worship and engage in jihad; it gives the sick person spiritual strength.
dualar.not: Reciting this supplication aloud beside the sick person serves both as a prayer and as a source of comfort.

dualar.baslik: Verses and Surahs to Recite During Illness
dualar.arapca: İhlas, Felak, Nas sureleri; Fatiha suresi
dualar.okunus: (İlgili sure ve ayetlerin okunuşu)
dualar.anlam: This entry is a reminder of the surahs and verses recited during illness. Translations of the relevant texts can be found in the surah and verse sections of the app.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Salam 50/2192 (al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, an-Nas); Abu Dawud, Tibb 19/3900 (al-Fatihah); Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Three times each morning and evening; additionally when experiencing discomfort
dualar.neZaman: When ill or experiencing pain
dualar.aciklama: According to the narration of our mother Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ became ill, he would recite Surahs al-Ikhlas, al-Falaq, and an-Nas into his hands, blow into them, and wipe his hands over his body; when his illness became severe, Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her) would do the same using his hand. Al-Fatihah was also recited as a means of ruqyah and healing in an authentic narration.
dualar.not: The basis of ruqyah is Quranic verses and authentic supplications; one should not go beyond these.

kategoriler.isim: Supplications for Funerals, Condolences, and Visiting Graves

dualar.baslik: Supplication to Recite When Calamity Strikes
dualar.arapca: إِنَّا لِلَّهِ وَإِنَّا إِلَيْهِ رَاجِعُونَ اللَّهُمَّ أْجُرْنِي فِي مُصِيبَتِي وَأَخْلِفْ لِي خَيْرًا مِنْهَا
dualar.okunus: İnnâ lillâhi ve innâ ileyhi râciûn. Allâhümmecürnî fî musîbetî ve ahlif lî hayran minhâ.
dualar.anlam: Indeed, we belong to Allah, and indeed, to Him we shall return. O Allah, reward me for this calamity and grant me something better in its place.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Jana'iz 4/918; the Quran, Surah al-Baqarah 156; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once when experiencing a calamity or loss, or receiving news of a death
dualar.neZaman: When receiving news of a death or facing a loss or calamity
dualar.aciklama: It was narrated from Umm Salamah (may Allah be pleased with her), the Mother of the Believers, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If a calamity befalls a Muslim and they recite this supplication, Allah will surely prepare a reward and recompense for them because of that calamity and give them something better than what He took away." (Muslim, Funerals 4/918). In verse 156 of al-Baqarah, these words are mentioned in the context of Allah's praise for those who are patient.
dualar.not: The phrase "İnnâ lillâhi ve innâ ileyhi râciûn" comes from the Qur'an (al-Baqarah 156), and reciting it when calamity strikes is commanded by the Qur'an; the second part is established by hadith, and reciting the two together is recommended.

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Forgiveness and Mercy for the Deceased
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَهُ وَارْحَمْهُ وَعَافِهِ وَاعْفُ عَنْهُ وَأَكْرِمْ نُزُلَهُ وَوَسِّعْ مَدْخَلَهُ وَاغْسِلْهُ بِالْمَاءِ وَالثَّلْجِ وَالْبَرَدِ وَنَقِّهِ مِنَ الْخَطَايَا كَمَا نَقَّيْتَ الثَّوْبَ الْأَبْيَضَ مِنَ الدَّنَسِ وَأَبْدِلْهُ دَارًا خَيْرًا مِنْ دَارِهِ وَأَهْلًا خَيْرًا مِنْ أَهْلِهِ وَزَوْجًا خَيْرًا مِنْ زَوْجِهِ وَأَدْخِلْهُ الْجَنَّةَ وَأَعِذْهُ مِنْ عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ وَعَذَابِ النَّارِ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümmağfir lehü verhemhü ve âfihî va'fü anhü ve ekrim nüzülehü ve vessi' medhalehu vağsilhü bi'l-mâi ve's-selci ve'l-beradi ve nakkıhî mine'l-hatâyâ kemâ nakkayte's-sevbe'l-ebyade mine'd-denesi ve ebdilhü dâran hayran min dârihî ve ehlen hayran min ehlihî ve zevcan hayran min zevcihî ve edhilhü'l-cennete ve e'ızhü min azâbi'l-kabri ve azâbi'n-nâr.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! Forgive them, have mercy on them, grant them well-being, and pardon them. Make their place of rest good and widen their entrance. Wash them with water, snow, and hail, and cleanse them of sins as You cleanse a white garment of dirt. Give them a home better than their home, a family better than their family, and a spouse better than their spouse. Admit them to Paradise and protect them from the punishment of the grave and the punishment of the Fire.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Funerals 16/963; Abu Dawud, Funerals 58/3201; Tirmidhi, Funerals 38/1025; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: During the funeral prayer (after the third takbir) and whenever praying for the deceased
dualar.neZaman: During the funeral prayer, after the deceased has been buried, and when visiting the grave
dualar.aciklama: It was narrated from Awf ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this supplication during a funeral prayer. (Muslim, Funerals 16/963). This is one of the best-known narrated supplications to be recited after the third takbir of the funeral prayer.
dualar.not: The supplication as written is for a man; for a woman, feminine forms are used, such as "lehâ" instead of "lehü" and "zevcihâ" instead of "zevcihî".

dualar.baslik: Supplication to Say to the Bereaved When Offering Condolences
dualar.arapca: إِنَّ لِلَّهِ مَا أَخَذَ وَلَهُ مَا أَعْطَى وَكُلُّ شَيْءٍ عِنْدَهُ بِأَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى فَلْتَصْبِرْ وَلْتَحْتَسِبْ
dualar.okunus: İnne lillâhi mâ ahaze ve lehû mâ a'tâ ve küllü şey'in indehû bi-ecelin müsemmâ, felyasbir ve'ltehtesib.
dualar.anlam: Allah is the One who takes and the One who gives. Everything has an appointed time with Him. So be patient and seek your reward from Allah.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Funerals 33/1284; Muslim, Funerals 14/923; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: Once to the bereaved when offering condolences
dualar.neZaman: Said when offering condolences to the relatives of someone who has died
dualar.aciklama: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ received news of his daughter's death, he sent this message to his daughter through Anas (may Allah be pleased with him), informing her that he would be patient and expect his reward from Allah. (Bukhari, Funerals 33/1284; Muslim, Funerals 14/923). These words express beautifully the Islamic understanding of submission that lies at the heart of offering condolences.
dualar.not: These words serve both to comfort and to provide spiritual guidance to the bereaved. As an additional expression of support, the supplication "Azîm ecre'llâhü leke" (May Allah grant you a great reward) may be added.

dualar.baslik: Comprehensive Supplication for Offering Condolences
dualar.arapca: أَعْظَمَ اللَّهُ أَجْرَكَ وَأَحْسَنَ عَزَاءَكَ وَغَفَرَ لِمَيِّتِكَ
dualar.okunus: A'zamelllâhü ecrak ve ahsene azâ'ek ve ğafera li-meyyitik.
dualar.anlam: May Allah increase your reward, grant you comfort, and forgive your deceased loved one.
dualar.kaynak: Nasa'i, Funerals 24/2089; Ibn Majah, Funerals 55/1601; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: Once to the bereaved when offering condolences
dualar.neZaman: When meeting the relatives of the deceased or paying a condolence visit
dualar.aciklama: This supplication brings together three essential requests: reward and comfort for the person struck by calamity, and forgiveness for the deceased. Scholars have stated that this supplication is an authentic and concise form for offering condolences.
dualar.not: Turkish expressions commonly used when offering condolences, such as "başınız sağ olsun" (my condolences) and "Allah sabır versin" (may Allah grant you patience), fall within the meaning of this supplication; however, the actual Sunnah is this Arabic formula.

dualar.baslik: Greeting and Supplication When Visiting Graves
dualar.arapca: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ أَهْلَ الدِّيَارِ مِنَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ وَالْمُسْلِمِينَ وَإِنَّا إِنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ بِكُمْ لَاحِقُونَ نَسْأَلُ اللَّهَ لَنَا وَلَكُمُ الْعَافِيَةَ
dualar.okunus: Es-selâmü aleyküm ehle'd-diyâri mine'l-mü'minîne ve'l-müslimîn, ve innâ inşâallâhü biküm lâhikûn. Nes'elüllâhe lenâ ve lekümü'l-âfiyeh.
dualar.anlam: Peace be upon you, believing and Muslim inhabitants of this abode. If Allah wills, we too will join you. We ask Allah to grant well-being to both us and you.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Funerals 104/975; Ibn Majah, Funerals 36/1547; Nasa'i, Funerals 102/2040; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: Once each time one enters a cemetery
dualar.neZaman: Upon entering a cemetery, at the start of a visit to the graves
dualar.aciklama: It was narrated from Aishah (may Allah be pleased with her), the Mother of the Believers, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would give this greeting when he went to the cemetery at night. (Muslim, Funerals 104/975). The permissibility of visiting graves and giving the greeting during a visit is established by hadith.
dualar.not: The purpose of visiting graves is to pray for the deceased, remember the Hereafter, and take a lesson from death. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Visit graves, for they remind you of death." (Muslim, Funerals 106/976).

dualar.baslik: Supplication at the Grave After Burial
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ اغْفِرْ لَهُ اللَّهُمَّ ثَبِّتْهُ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümmeğfir leh. Allâhümme sebbidhü.
dualar.anlam: O Allah, forgive them. O Allah, grant them steadfastness.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Funerals 69/3221; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: Once at the graveside immediately after burial
dualar.neZaman: When standing at the grave and making supplication after the deceased has been buried
dualar.aciklama: After burying a deceased person, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would stand at the grave and say: "Seek forgiveness for your brother and ask Allah to grant him steadfastness in answering the questions, for he is being questioned now." (Abu Dawud, Funerals 69/3221). More comprehensive supplications may also be made after the short supplication.
dualar.not: Making supplication at the graveside after burial and sitting for a while (reciting the Qur'an) is established by the Sunnah.

dualar.baslik: Supplication Upon Waking (Short)
dualar.arapca: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي أَحْيَانَا بَعْدَ مَا أَمَاتَنَا وَإِلَيْهِ النُّشُورُ
dualar.okunus: Elhamdü lillâhillezî ahyânâ ba'de mâ emâtenâ ve ileyhi'n-nüşûr.
dualar.anlam: Praise be to Allah, who gave us life after death. To Him is the return.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Supplications 7-8, 16; Muslim, Remembrance 59; Abu Dawud, Manners 98; Tirmidhi, Supplications 28; Ibn Majah, Supplications 17; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: Once every morning upon waking from sleep
dualar.neZaman: Upon waking from sleep, as soon as one opens one's eyes
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ would recite this supplication when he woke from sleep. Sleep is described in hadiths as "the lesser death"; this supplication reminds us that every morning brings the blessing of life anew.
dualar.not: It is Sunnah to recite it as soon as one opens one's eyes, before getting out of bed.

dualar.baslik: Supplication Upon Waking (Comprehensive — Narrated by Abu Hurayrah)
dualar.arapca: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ الَّذِي عَافَانِي فِي جَسَدِي وَرَدَّ عَلَيَّ رُوحِي وَأَذِنَ لِي بِذِكْرِهِ
dualar.okunus: Elhamdü lillâhillezî âfânî fî cesedî ve redde aleyye rûhî ve ezine lî bi-zikrih.
dualar.anlam: Praise be to Allah, who granted my body well-being, returned my soul to me, and gave me the opportunity to remember Him.
dualar.kaynak: Tirmidhi, Supplications 20/3401; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: Once every morning upon waking from sleep
dualar.neZaman: Upon waking from sleep
dualar.aciklama: It was narrated from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you wake from sleep, recite this supplication." This supplication expresses gratitude for the blessings of bodily health, the return of the soul, and remembrance of Allah.
dualar.not: It may be recited together with the short supplication or in its place. Both are in accordance with the Sunnah.

dualar.baslik: Supplication When Getting Dressed
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ خَيْرِهِ وَخَيْرِ مَا هُوَ لَهُ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهِ وَشَرِّ مَا هُوَ لَهُ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme innî es'elüke min hayrihî ve hayri mâ hüve leh, ve eûzü bike min şerrihî ve şerri mâ hüve leh.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! I ask You for the good of this garment and the good of whatever it was made for. I seek refuge in You from its evil and the evil of whatever it was made for.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Clothing 1/4020; Tirmidhi, Supplications 107/3560; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: Once when getting dressed
dualar.neZaman: When putting on any garment, especially a new one
dualar.aciklama: Narrated by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him): When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ put on a garment such as a shirt, cloak, or turban, he would recite this supplication. (Abu Dawud, Libas 1/4020; Tirmidhi, Da'awat 107/3560).
dualar.not: It is also Sunnah to say "Bismillâh" when taking off a garment. (Tirmidhi, 2/505)

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Someone Wearing New Clothes
dualar.arapca: تُبْلِي وَيُخْلِفُ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى
dualar.okunus: Tüblî ve yuhlifullâhü te'âlâ.
dualar.anlam: May this garment wear out and may Allah Most High give you a new one in its place.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Libas 1/4020; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: Once when speaking to someone wearing new clothes
dualar.neZaman: When you see someone wearing new clothes
dualar.aciklama: It is Sunnah to wish someone well with this supplication when they wear new clothes. The person who hears it may reply, "Ve ente fe-eczelellâhü leke" (May Allah grant you the same).
dualar.not: Another narration states that one may also say, "Elbes cedîden ve a'yiş hamîden ve müt şehîden" (May you wear new clothes, live praising Allah, and die as a martyr). (Ibn Majah, 2/1178)

kategoriler.isim: Going to, Entering, and Leaving the Mosque

dualar.baslik: Supplication When Going to the Mosque
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ اجْعَلْ فِي قَلْبِي نُورًا وَفِي لِسَانِي نُورًا وَاجْعَلْ فِي سَمْعِي نُورًا وَاجْعَلْ فِي بَصَرِي نُورًا وَاجْعَلْ مِنْ خَلْفِي نُورًا وَمِنْ أَمَامِي نُورًا وَاجْعَلْ مِنْ فَوْقِي نُورًا وَمِنْ تَحْتِي نُورًا اللَّهُمَّ أَعْطِنِي نُورًا
dualar.okunus: Allâhümmec'al fî kalbî nûran ve fî lisânî nûran vec'al fî sem'î nûran vec'al fî basarî nûran vec'al min halfî nûran ve min emâmî nûran vec'al min fevkî nûran ve min tahtî nûran, Allâhümme a'tinî nûrâ.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! Put light in my heart, light on my tongue, light in my ears, and light in my eyes. Place light behind me, light before me, light above me, and light beneath me. O Allah, grant me light.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Da'awat 6/6316; Muslim, Musafirin 181/763; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: Once each time one goes to the mosque
dualar.neZaman: While walking toward the mosque
dualar.aciklama: Narrated by Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him): One night, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ recited this supplication as he left Aisha's room and walked toward the mosque. (Bukhari, Da'awat 6/6316; Muslim, Musafirin 181/763).
dualar.not: When going to the mosque, it is also Sunnah to enter with the right foot and say the basmala.

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Entering the Mosque
dualar.arapca: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ اللَّهُمَّ افْتَحْ لِي أَبْوَابَ رَحْمَتِكَ
dualar.okunus: Bismillâhi ve's-salâtu ve's-selâmu alâ rasûlillâh. Allâhümmeftah lî ebvâbe rahmetik.
dualar.anlam: In the name of Allah. May blessings and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah! Open the doors of Your mercy for me.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Musafirin 68/713; Abu Dawud, Salat 22/465; Ibn Majah, Masajid 14/771; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: Once each time one enters the mosque
dualar.neZaman: When entering through the mosque door, stepping in with the right foot
dualar.aciklama: This supplication is recited when entering the mosque with the right foot. Asking for the doors of mercy to be opened strengthens the spiritual dimension of salah and worship.
dualar.not: It is Sunnah to enter the mosque with the right foot.

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Leaving the Mosque
dualar.arapca: بِسْمِ اللَّهِ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى رَسُولِ اللَّهِ اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ اللَّهُمَّ اعْصِمْنِي مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ
dualar.okunus: Bismillâhi ve's-salâtu ve's-selâmu alâ rasûlillâh. Allâhümme innî es'elüke min fadlik. Allâhümme'sımnî mine'ş-şeytâni'r-racîm.
dualar.anlam: In the name of Allah. May blessings and peace be upon the Messenger of Allah. O Allah! I ask You for Your bounty. O Allah! Protect me from the accursed devil.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Tahajjud 25/1/625; Muslim, Musafirin 68/713; Ibn Majah, Masajid 14/772; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: Once each time one leaves the mosque
dualar.neZaman: When leaving through the mosque door, stepping out with the left foot
dualar.aciklama: It is Sunnah to leave the mosque with the left foot and recite this supplication. The supplication includes asking Allah for His bounty in worldly affairs and seeking protection from the devil when going out.
dualar.not: It is Sunnah to leave the mosque with the left foot; this supplication is also recited at that time.

dualar.baslik: Repeating the Adhan and Sending Blessings
dualar.arapca: (Müezzinin her cümlesini tekrar et; "Hayye ale's-salâh" ve "Hayye ale'l-felâh" duydukta "Lâ havle ve lâ kuvvete illâ billâh" de)
dualar.okunus: Müezzin ne diyorsa aynısını tekrar et; "Hayye ale's-salâh" ve "Hayye ale'l-felâh" için "Lâ havle ve lâ kuvvete illâ billâh" de.
dualar.anlam: There is no power or strength except with Allah's help.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Adhan 7/611; Muslim, Salat 11/383; Abu Dawud, Salat 37/527; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: Whenever the adhan is called
dualar.neZaman: While the adhan is being called, as each phrase is said
dualar.aciklama: Narrated by Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you hear the adhan, repeat what the muezzin says." (Bukhari, Adhan 7/611; Muslim, Salat 11/383). At the phrases "Hayye ale's-salâh" and "Hayye ale'l-felâh", one says "Lâ havle ve lâ kuvvete illâ billâh". (Muslim, Salat 11/385).
dualar.not: If a person who hears the adhan is in a quiet setting, it is recommended to repeat it along with the muezzin.

dualar.baslik: Supplication After the Adhan
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ رَبَّ هَٰذِهِ الدَّعْوَةِ التَّامَّةِ وَالصَّلَاةِ الْقَائِمَةِ آتِ مُحَمَّدًا الْوَسِيلَةَ وَالْفَضِيلَةَ وَابْعَثْهُ مَقَامًا مَحْمُودًا الَّذِي وَعَدْتَهُ
