dualar.okunus: Allâhümme rabbe hâzihi'd-da'veti't-tâmmeti ve's-salâti'l-kâimeti âti Muhammeden el-vesîlete ve'l-fadîlete ve'b'ashü makâmen mahmûdeni'llezî va'adteh.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! Lord of this perfect call and the prayer being established! Grant Muhammad the means of nearness and virtue, and raise him to the praised station You have promised him.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Adhan 8/614; Abu Dawud, Salat 37/529; Tirmidhi, Salat 43/211; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: Once after each adhan ends
dualar.neZaman: As soon as the adhan ends, immediately after sending blessings upon the Prophet
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you hear the muezzin, repeat what he says, then send blessings upon me; then ask Allah to grant me the means of nearness. The means of nearness is a station in Paradise that will be granted to only one of His servants, and I hope that I will be that servant. Whoever asks for the means of nearness for me will be entitled to my intercession." (Muslim, Salat 11/384).
dualar.not: It is recommended to recite this supplication before performing the Sunnah prayer after the adhan.

dualar.baslik: Supplication for the Istikhara Prayer
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْتَخِيرُكَ بِعِلْمِكَ وَأَسْتَقْدِرُكَ بِقُدْرَتِكَ وَأَسْأَلُكَ مِنْ فَضْلِكَ الْعَظِيمِ فَإِنَّكَ تَقْدِرُ وَلَا أَقْدِرُ وَتَعْلَمُ وَلَا أَعْلَمُ وَأَنْتَ عَلَّامُ الْغُيُوبِ اللَّهُمَّ إِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَٰذَا الْأَمْرَ خَيْرٌ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي فَاقْدُرْهُ لِي وَيَسِّرْهُ لِي ثُمَّ بَارِكْ لِي فِيهِ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ تَعْلَمُ أَنَّ هَٰذَا الْأَمْرَ شَرٌّ لِي فِي دِينِي وَمَعَاشِي وَعَاقِبَةِ أَمْرِي فَاصْرِفْهُ عَنِّي وَاصْرِفْنِي عَنْهُ وَاقْدُرْ لِيَ الْخَيْرَ حَيْثُ كَانَ ثُمَّ أَرْضِنِي بِهِ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme innî estehîruke bi-ilmike ve estakdiruke bi-kudretike ve es'elüke min fadlike'l-azîm. Fe-inneke takdiru ve lâ akdiru ve ta'lemü ve lâ a'lemü ve ente allâmü'l-ğuyûb. Allâhümme in künte ta'lemü enne hâze'l-emre hayrun lî fî dînî ve meâşî ve âkıbeti emrî fekdürhü lî ve yessirhu lî sümme bârik lî fîh. Ve in künte ta'lemü enne hâze'l-emre şerrun lî fî dînî ve meâşî ve âkıbeti emrî fasrifhü annî vasrifnî anhü vakdür liye'l-hayre haysu kâne sümme ardınî bih.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! By Your knowledge, I ask You for what is best, and by Your power, I ask You for strength, and I ask You from Your great bounty. For You have power and I do not; You know and I do not; and You know the unseen best. O Allah! If You know that this matter is good for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affairs, then ordain it for me, make it easy for me, and bless me in it. If You know that this matter is bad for me in my religion, my livelihood, and the outcome of my affairs, then turn it away from me and turn me away from it. Ordain for me what is good wherever it may be; then make me content with it.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Tahajjud 28/6382; Da'awat 48; Tawhid 10/7390; Abu Dawud, Salat 358/1538; Tirmidhi, Witr 18/480; Nasa'i, Nikah 25; Ibn Majah, Iqamah 188/1383; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: Once before an important decision (may be repeated)
dualar.neZaman: Before an important matter or decision, after performing 2 rak'ahs of non-obligatory prayer
dualar.aciklama: Narrated by Jabir ibn Abdillah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to teach us istikhara for every important matter as he would teach us a surah from the Qur'an. (Bukhari, Tahajjud 28/6382). Istikhara is performed by reciting this supplication after 2 rak'ahs of voluntary prayer; during the supplication, when saying "hâze'l-emr" (this matter), the matter one intends to pursue is mentioned in the heart or aloud.
dualar.not: There is no requirement to see a dream after istikhara; the feeling of peace or unease that arises in the heart is taken as guidance. If one has difficulty making a decision, istikhara may be repeated.

kategoriler.isim: When Having a Nightmare or Bad Dream

dualar.baslik: Seeking Protection from a Bad Dream
dualar.arapca: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ وَمِنْ شَرِّ هَٰذِهِ الرُّؤْيَا
dualar.okunus: Eûzü billâhi mine'ş-şeytâni'r-racîm ve min şerri hâzihi'r-rü'yâ.
dualar.anlam: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed devil and from the evil of this dream.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Ru'ya 3/2261; Abu Dawud, Adab 88/5021; Tirmidhi, Ru'ya 3/2277; Ibn Majah, Ta'bir 3/3909; Hisnü'l-Müslim
dualar.tekrar: When one has a bad dream or nightmare
dualar.neZaman: Immediately upon waking from a bad or frightening dream
dualar.aciklama: Narrated by Abu Qatadah (may Allah be pleased with him): The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A good dream is from Allah, and a bad dream is from the devil. If any of you sees a dream they dislike, let them spit to their left three times, seek refuge in Allah from the devil, and change the side on which they were sleeping. This dream will not harm them, and they should not tell anyone about it." (Muslim, Ru'ya 3/2261; Bukhari, Ta'bir 3/6985).
dualar.not: When one has a bad dream, lightly spitting to the left, seeking refuge in Allah, and changing one's sleeping position are established by hadith. Performing salah is also mentioned in some narrations or in the advice of scholars.

dualar.baslik: Seeking Protection from Satan When Angry
dualar.arapca: أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ مِنَ الشَّيْطَانِ الرَّجِيمِ
dualar.okunus: Eûzü billâhi mine'ş-şeytâni'r-racîm.
dualar.anlam: I seek refuge in Allah from the accursed Satan.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Adab 76/6115; Muslim, Birr 109/2610; Abu Dawud, Adab 4/4781; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: When feeling angry; may be repeated as needed
dualar.neZaman: Immediately upon feeling angry
dualar.aciklama: It is narrated from Sulayman ibn Surad (may Allah be pleased with him) that two men became angry with each other in the presence of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. The face of one of them turned red. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I know a phrase that drives Satan away. If he said it, what he feels inside would go away: 'Eûzü billâhi mine'ş-şeytâni'r-racîm.'" (Bukhari, Adab 76/6115; Muslim, Birr 109/2610).
dualar.not: When angry, sitting down if standing, lying down if sitting, performing wudu, and remaining silent are also recommendations from the Sunnah.

dualar.baslik: Praising Allah After Sneezing
dualar.arapca: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ
dualar.okunus: Elhamdülillâh. (veya: Elhamdü lillâhi alâ külli hâl)
dualar.anlam: Praise be to Allah. (Or: Praise be to Allah in all circumstances.)
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Adab 126/6224; Abu Dawud, Adab 91/5028; Tirmidhi, Adab 3/2742; Ibn Majah, Adab 20/3714; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once after each sneeze
dualar.neZaman: Immediately after sneezing
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah loves sneezing and dislikes yawning. If one of you sneezes and says 'Elhamdülillâh', every Muslim who hears it should say 'Yerhamükellâh'." (Bukhari, Adab 126/6224; Muslim, Zuhd 54/2994). The wording "Elhamdü lillâhi alâ külli hâl" (Praise be to Allah in all circumstances) also appears in Abu Dawud and Tirmidhi.
dualar.not: It is proper etiquette to cover one's mouth with one's hand or a cloth when sneezing.

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Someone Who Sneezes (Tashmit)
dualar.arapca: يَرْحَمُكَ اللَّهُ
dualar.okunus: Yerhamükellâh.
dualar.anlam: May Allah have mercy on you.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Adab 126/6224; Muslim, Zuhd 54/2994; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once after the person who sneezed says "Elhamdülillâh"
dualar.neZaman: When someone near you sneezes and praises Allah
dualar.aciklama: This response is called 'tashmit'. If the person who sneezes praises Allah, it is Sunnah for the Muslim who hears it to say 'Yerhamükellâh'; some scholars have regarded it as strongly obligatory.
dualar.not: If the person who sneezes does not say "Elhamdülillâh", tashmit is not required; however, one may say "Elhamdülillâh" as a reminder.

dualar.baslik: Response to Tashmit
dualar.arapca: يَهْدِيكُمُ اللَّهُ وَيُصْلِحُ بَالَكُمْ
dualar.okunus: Yehdîkümüllâhü ve yuslihu bâleküm.
dualar.anlam: May Allah guide you and set your affairs right.
dualar.kaynak: Bukhari, Adab 126/6224; Abu Dawud, Adab 91/5031; Tirmidhi, Adab 3/2742; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once when "Yerhamükellâh" is said
dualar.neZaman: As a response when "Yerhamükellâh" is said to the person who sneezed
dualar.aciklama: The etiquette of sneezing has three stages: The person who sneezes says "Elhamdülillâh" → the person nearby says "Yerhamükellâh" → the person who sneezed says "Yehdîkümüllâhü ve yuslihu bâleküm". This three-part Sunnah is established in Bukhari. (Bukhari, Adab 126/6224).
dualar.not: Further sneezing after three times is considered a sign of a cold; tashmit is not required.

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Entering a Market
dualar.arapca: لَا إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَهُوَ حَيٌّ لَا يَمُوتُ بِيَدِهِ الْخَيْرُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
dualar.okunus: Lâ ilâhe illallâhü vahdehû lâ şerîke leh, lehü'l-mülkü ve lehü'l-hamdü yuhyî ve yümît, ve hüve hayyün lâ yemûtü bi-yedihi'l-hayr, ve hüve alâ külli şey'in kadîr.
dualar.anlam: There is no true god but Allah. He is One and has no partner. Sovereignty is His, and all praise belongs to Him. He gives life and causes death. He is the Ever-Living and does not die. All good is in His hand. He has power over all things.
dualar.kaynak: Tirmidhi, Da'awat 79/3428 (hasan-gharib); Ibn Majah, Tijarat 1/2235; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.derece: Hasan-gharib (Tirmidhi; there are differing assessments of its chain of narration)
dualar.tekrar: Once each time one enters a market or bazaar
dualar.neZaman: When entering places such as markets, bazaars, and shopping centres
dualar.aciklama: The narration about reciting this dhikr in places such as markets and bazaars, where heedlessness is widespread, appears in Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. Although there are differing assessments of the hadith's chain of narration, reciting it in hope of its virtue has been common.
dualar.not: Hadith scholars have assessed this narration differently. For this reason, it is more appropriate to recite it with caution and in hope of its virtue, without presenting its promise as certain.

dualar.baslik: Congratulations and Supplication for Someone Who Marries
dualar.arapca: بَارَكَ اللَّهُ لَكَ وَبَارَكَ عَلَيْكَ وَجَمَعَ بَيْنَكُمَا فِي خَيْرٍ
dualar.okunus: Bârekallâhü lek ve bâreke aleyk ve cemea beynekümâ fî hayr.
dualar.anlam: May Allah bless you, send blessings upon you, and bring the two of you together in goodness.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Nikah 32/2130; Tirmidhi, Nikah 8/1091 (hasan-sahih); Ibn Majah, Nikah 23/1905; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once upon meeting the person who has married
dualar.neZaman: When learning that someone has married or meeting the person who has married
dualar.aciklama: It is narrated from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would offer this supplication for a person who had married. (Abu Dawud, Nikah 32/2130; Tirmidhi, Nikah 8/1091). This supplication is the Sunnah form of the commonly expressed wish for a blessed marriage and includes a prayer for blessing, goodness, and togetherness.
dualar.not: When someone receives this supplication, they may say "Ve leke mislü zâlik" (And the same to you).

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Blessing for One's Spouse on the First Night
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَسْأَلُكَ خَيْرَهَا وَخَيْرَ مَا جَبَلْتَهَا عَلَيْهِ وَأَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ شَرِّهَا وَشَرِّ مَا جَبَلْتَهَا عَلَيْهِ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme innî es'elüke hayrehâ ve hayra mâ cebeltehâ aleyh, ve eûzü bike min şerrihâ ve şerri mâ cebeltehâ aleyh.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! I ask You for the good in her and the good You have placed in her nature. I seek refuge in You from the evil in her and the evil You have placed in her nature.
dualar.kaynak: Abu Dawud, Nikah 32/2160; Ibn Majah, Nikah 23/1918; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once when first coming together with one's spouse
dualar.neZaman: On the wedding night, when first meeting one's spouse, while placing a hand on her forehead and supplicating
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you marries a woman, let him hold her forehead and say the basmalah, then recite this supplication." (Abu Dawud, Nikah 32/2160; Ibn Majah, Nikah 23/1918). This practice and supplication are for the husband; the wife may recite the same supplication for her husband using the pronoun "hü" (he/him).
dualar.not: For a man, "hayrehü" is recited instead of "hayrehâ".

kategoriler.isim: Seeking Protection from the Evil of the Dajjal

dualar.baslik: Supplication for Protection from Four Things (Before the Salam in Salah)
dualar.arapca: اللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوذُ بِكَ مِنْ عَذَابِ جَهَنَّمَ وَمِنْ عَذَابِ الْقَبْرِ وَمِنْ فِتْنَةِ الْمَحْيَا وَالْمَمَاتِ وَمِنْ شَرِّ فِتْنَةِ الْمَسِيحِ الدَّجَّالِ
dualar.okunus: Allâhümme innî eûzü bike min azâbi cehenneme ve min azâbi'l-kabri ve min fitneti'l-mahyâ ve'l-memâti ve min şerri fitneti'l-mesîhi'd-deccâl.
dualar.anlam: O Allah! I seek refuge in You from the punishment of Hell, the punishment of the grave, the trials of life and death, and the evil of the trial of the false messiah, the Dajjal.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Masajid 128/588; Bukhari, Adhan 149/1377; Abu Dawud, Salat 183/983; Nasa'i, Sahw 66/1309; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Once during the tashahhud of every salah, before saying the salam
dualar.neZaman: During the final sitting of salah, after the Tahiyyat and salawat, immediately before saying the salam
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you completes the tashahhud, let him seek refuge in Allah from four things." (Muslim, Masajid 128/588). This is one of the most comprehensive supplications for protection that the Messenger of Allah regularly recited during salah, and it directly addresses the trial of the Dajjal.
dualar.not: This supplication is related to the "Supplications before the salam in salah" section in category A; it is also included here in the context of protection from the Dajjal.

dualar.baslik: The First 10 Verses of Surah al-Kahf
dualar.arapca: (Kehf Suresi, 1-10. ayetler)
dualar.okunus: (Kehf Suresinin ilk 10 ayeti)
dualar.anlam: This entry is a reminder to recite the first 10 verses of Surah al-Kahf. The translation of the verses can be viewed on the relevant surah screen in the app.
dualar.kaynak: Muslim, Musafirin 257/809; Abu Dawud, Malahim 14/4323; Nasa'i, Salat al-Layl 19; Hisn al-Muslim
dualar.tekrar: Especially on Fridays; regularly
dualar.neZaman: Every Friday; as part of the morning or evening adhkar
dualar.aciklama: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever memorizes ten verses from the beginning of Surah al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal." (Muslim, Musafirin 257/809; Abu Dawud, Malahim 14/4323). The virtue of reciting Surah al-Kahf on Friday is also established by authentic hadiths. The first 10 verses of this surah explain, through the story of the Companions of the Cave, that Allah protects His servants from the evil of oppression.
dualar.not: Some narrations also mention the "last 10 verses"; however, the narration mentioning the "first 10 verses" is stronger in Muslim.
